'''Claude Makélélé Sinda''' ({{IPA|fr|klod makele'le}}; born 18 February 1973) is a French [[Manager (association football)|football manager]] and former [[Football player|professional player]] who played as a [[defensive midfielder]]. He last managed [[Super League Greece]] club [[Asteras Tripolis F.C.|Asteras Tripolis]]. Regarded as one of the greatest defensive midfielders of all time,<ref>{{cite news |last= |first= |date=13 February 2018 |title=Ranked! The 101 greatest football players of the last 25 years: full list |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/101-greatest-football-players-last-25-years-full-list |accessdate=22 December 2023 |work=[[FourFourTwo]] |edition=253}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bishop |first=Callum |date=2024-10-08 |title=The 20 greatest midfielders in football history have been ranked - Iniesta 6th |url=https://www.givemesport.com/greatest-midfielders-in-football-history/ |access-date=2024-11-30 |website=GiveMeSport |language=en}}</ref> Makélélé has been credited with redefining the defensive midfield role in English football, especially during the [[2004–05 FA Premier League]] season, where he played a key role in helping Chelsea win the title with 95 points. In homage, the defensive midfield position is sometimes colloquially known as the "Makélélé Role".<ref name="Makelele role">{{cite news |last=Wallace |first=Sam |date=24 February 2007 |title=Doing a Makelele – so good they named it after him |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/news-and-comment/doing-a-makelele--so-good-they-named-it-after-him-437647.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101127033517/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/news-and-comment/doing-a-makelele--so-good-they-named-it-after-him-437647.html |archive-date=27 November 2010 |newspaper=The Independent |location=London}}</ref><ref name="zonalmarking">{{cite web |date=30 July 2010 |title=What does a central midfielder do in 2010? |url=http://www.zonalmarking.net/2010/07/30/central-midfield-role/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160729225620/http://www.zonalmarking.net/2010/07/30/central-midfield-role/ |archive-date=29 July 2016 |access-date=13 July 2016 |website=ZonalMarking.net}}</ref>

In his playing career, which ended at [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]], Makélélé also played for [[FC Nantes|Nantes]], [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]], [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]], [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and Chelsea. He won league titles in France, Spain and England, as well as the [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League]] during his time with Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite news |title=15 years on from Zidane's final wonder goal |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0239-0e9c7f74cced-4d02500f3f8e-1000--15-years-on-from-zidane-s-final-wonder-goal/ |website=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=15 May 2017 |access-date=23 September 2018 }}</ref> Furthermore, Makélélé was once selected in the [[FIFPRO#FIFA FIFPRO Men's World 11|FIFPRO Men's World 11]] while playing for Chelsea.<ref>{{Cite news |title=FIFPro World XI: Which 11 players made FIFA's team of the year for 2014? |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11096/9643492/fifpro-world-xi-which-11-players-made-fifas-team-of-the-year-for-2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250601213801/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11096/9643492/fifpro-world-xi-which-11-players-made-fifas-team-of-the-year-for-2014 |archive-date=1 June 2025 |access-date=2025-06-22 |work=Sky Sports |language=en-GB |url-status=live }}</ref>

Born in Zaire, Makélélé was a French international for 13 years and was part of the [[France national football team|France national team]] which reached the final of the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]]. He also represented his nation at the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]], two [[UEFA European Championship]]s and the [[Football at the 1996 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|1996 Summer Olympics]].

After retiring from playing, Makélélé went into coaching and technical staff roles. He has been manager at [[SC Bastia|Bastia]], [[K.A.S. Eupen|Eupen]] and [[Asteras Tripolis F.C.|Asteras Tripolis]]; assistant manager at Paris Saint-Germain and Swansea; a youth coach and technical mentor at Chelsea; and technical director at Monaco.

==Club career==
===Early career===
Makélélé was born in [[Kinshasa]], Zaire (now the Democratic Republic of the Congo). "Makélélé" means "noises" in [[Swahili|Lingala]],<ref>{{cite news |first=Chumvi |last=Mtembezi |title=Swahili Stars |url=http://chumvi.tripod.com/nyota.html |access-date=30 November 2008 |year=2002 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080718150741/http://chumvi.tripod.com/nyota.html |archive-date=18 July 2008}}</ref> one of the languages spoken in the country. He moved to [[Savigny-le-Temple]], a suburb of Paris in Seine-et-Marne, in 1977, when he was four years old. His father, André-Joseph Makélélé, was also a football player. He represented [[DR Congo national football team|DR Congo]], and ended his career in the third division of Belgium with [[Union Royale Namur]].<ref>{{cite web |date=19 December 2017 |title=À la gloire du père, la saga Makélélé |trans-title=To the glory of the father, the Makélélé saga |url=https://sportmagazine.levif.be/sport/foot-national/a-la-gloire-du-pere-la-saga-makelele/article-normal-1065703.html?cookie_check=1564784776 |access-date=2 August 2019 |publisher=Sport Magazine |language=fr}}</ref>

At age 15, Makélélé signed for [[Sporting Melun-Dammarie 77]]. He played one year there, and left at the age of 16, when he joined the training centre of Brest-Armorique in [[Brittany]]. Despite maturing in [[Stade Brestois|Brest]], but it was in the city of [[Nantes]] where he would sign a professional contract. Makélélé was recruited by [[FC Nantes|Nantes]] in December 1991, when he was still 18&nbsp;years old. [[Robert Budzynski]], Nantes' sporting director, stated that once he had discovered Makélélé in Brest, he was sure he would become the new [[Emmanuel Petit]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Iyer|first=Vignesh|date=2012-07-27|title=Claude Makelele ai??i?? The Position, The Player And The Man|url=http://www.thehardtackle.com/2012/claude-makelele-aii-the-position-the-player-and-the-man/|access-date=2021-07-12|website=Thehardtackle.com|language=en-US}}</ref>

At the beginning of the 1992–93 season, Makélélé was already in the Nantes first-team, then playing in the [[Ligue 1|French first division]]. He played at Nantes for five seasons, winning the French championship in 1995 and helped the club to the semi-final of the [[UEFA Champions League]] the following season. This earned him a move to [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] for whom he played for one season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-04-02 |title=From Ligue 1 to Superstardom: Claude Makelele, a real Galactico |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/from-ligue-1-to-superstardom-claude-makelele---real-galactico/2s5ta738f9221dm97qhgqdkki |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=www.goal.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Celta Vigo===
Makélélé was transferred to [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]] where he spent two successful seasons at the [[Galicia (Spain)|Galician]] club. While playing alongside [[Aleksandr Mostovoi]], [[Valeri Karpin]], [[Haim Revivo]] and [[Míchel Salgado]], Celta achieved historic victories such as 4–1 against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and 4–0 against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the [[UEFA Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celta Vigo - Juventus 4:0 (Europa League 1999/2000, Ottavi di finale) |trans-title=Celta Vigo - Juventus 4:0 (Europa League 1999/2000, Round of 16) |url=https://www.calcio.com/cronaca_partita/europa-league-1999-2000-achtelfinale-celta-vigo-juventus/ |access-date=2021-07-12 |website=calcio.com |language=it}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
{{Quote box
|quote = …we knew that [[Zinedine Zidane|Zidane]], [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]], and [[Luís Figo|Figo]] didn't track back, so we had to put a guy in front of the [[Defender (association football)|back four]] who would defend.
|source = [[Arrigo Sacchi]] describes [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]'s need for a holding midfielder.<ref name=pyramid>{{cite book |last1=Wilson |first1=Jonathan |title=Inverting the Pyramid |date=2013 |publisher=Nation Books |isbn=9781568589633}}</ref>
|quoted = 1
|align = right
|width = 23em
}}
In summer 2000, while Makélélé's former teammate at Nantes [[Christian Karembeu]] left [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] for [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]], he was snapped up by the Spanish capital club. Makélélé's transfer was controversial, as Celta did not want to sell Makélélé unless a substantial improvement on their offer was made. Makélélé refused to train until there was resolution of his contract. Finally, Celta were reluctantly forced to sell him for €14 million, far less than their valuation of the player and only after a falsified police report was made by his agent, Marc Roger.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.90min.com/posts/5646173-former-agent-reveals-the-shocking-events-that-led-to-claude-makelele-joining-real-madrid-from-celta|title=Former Agent Reveals the Shocking Events That Led to Claude Makelele Joining Real Madrid From Celta|publisher=90 Min|date=8 October 2017|access-date=2 August 2019|archive-date=5 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200805173245/https://www.90min.com/posts/5646173-former-agent-reveals-the-shocking-events-that-led-to-claude-makelele-joining-real-madrid-from-celta|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At Real, Makélélé added to his medal tally, winning two Spanish [[La Liga]] championships, the Champions League, the [[Supercopa de España]], the [[UEFA Super Cup]] and the [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]]. As an ever-present in [[Vicente del Bosque]]'s Real Madrid side, Makélélé also established himself as one of the best [[defensive midfielder]]s in the world.<ref name="Galactico">{{cite web |date=4 February 2017 |title=From Ligue 1 to Superstardom: Claude Makelele - Real Galactico |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/from-ligue-1-to-superstardom-claude-makelele-real-galactico/2s5ta738f9221dm97qhgqdkki |access-date=2 August 2019 |publisher=Goal}}</ref>

Despite his value to the team, however, Makélélé was one of its most (relatively) under-paid members, earning a fraction of that paid to teammates like [[Zinedine Zidane]], [[Luís Figo]], [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]], [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]], [[Roberto Carlos]], [[Steve McManaman]], and [[Guti]]. In the summer of 2003, feeling that his position at the club was insecure after the shock dismissal of Del Bosque and the arrival of [[David Beckham]], and encouraged by teammates Zidane, Raúl, McManaman and [[Fernando Morientes]], Makélélé decided to ask for an improved contract. The Real management flatly refused to consider his request.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.chinadaily.com.cn/en/doc/2003-08/15/content_255147.htm |title=Unhappy Makelele continues pay rise rebellion |newspaper=China Daily |location=Beijing |date=15 August 2003 |access-date=26 January 2019}}</ref> Upset, Makélélé handed in a transfer request, whereupon he was signed by [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. Club president [[Florentino Pérez]] poured scorn on Makélélé's footballing abilities and said that Makélélé would not be missed:

{{blockquote|He wasn't a header of the ball and he rarely passed the ball more than three metres. Younger players will arrive who will cause Makélélé to be forgotten.<ref name="Perez has parting shot at Makelele">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2003/sep/11/newsstory.sport9 |title=Perez has parting shot at Makelele |first=Richard |last=Stevens |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=11 September 2003 |access-date=26 January 2019}}</ref>}}

Pérez's opinion differed from that of players like Zidane, who remarked the following after Makélélé was sold and Beckham was bought:<ref>{{Cite news |last=Williams |first=Richard |date=2008-05-20 |title=Only Cole demurs as Chelsea cheer Makelele mastery |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2008/may/20/onlycoledemursaschelseach |access-date=2025-10-25 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

{{quote|Why put another layer of gold paint on the [[Bentley]] when you are losing the entire engine?}}

In his autobiography, published in 2006, McManaman described Makélélé as the most important and yet least appreciated midfielder at Real. Retired former Real Madrid player and captain [[Fernando Hierro]] also criticised Pérez for both Makélélé's departure and the manner of his departure, saying:

{{blockquote|I think Claude has this kind of gift – he's been the best player in the team for years but people just don't notice him, don't notice what he does. But you ask anyone at Real Madrid during the years we were talking about and they will tell you he was the best player at Real. We all knew, the players all knew he was the most important. The loss of Makélélé was the beginning of the end for Los Galacticos. You can see that it was also the beginning of a new dawn for Chelsea. He was the base, the key and I think he is the same to Chelsea now.<ref name=fernandohierro>{{cite news |date=30 April 2005 |url=http://www.fernandohierro.com/news/63.htm |title=Hierro's hunger drives Bolton to brink of history |publisher=Fernando Hierro.com |access-date=30 March 2007 |archive-date=31 October 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101031001113/http://www.fernandohierro.com/news/63.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>}}

===Chelsea===
[[File:Claude Makélélé.jpg|thumb|upright|Makélélé in 2008]]
[[File:Alex Makélélé.jpg|thumb|upright|Makélélé (right) with [[Alex (footballer, born June 1982)|Alex]] in 2008]]
In the summer of 2003, Makélélé signed for Chelsea for [[Pound sterling|£]]16.8 million, where then manager [[Claudio Ranieri]] proclaimed that Makélélé would be the "battery" of the team.<ref name=battery>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2421303/Makelele-the-battery-in-Chelsea-Rolex.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2421303/Makelele-the-battery-in-Chelsea-Rolex.html |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=Makelele the battery in Chelsea Rolex |first=Sarah |last=Edworthy |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=13 September 2003 |access-date=26 January 2019}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

====2003–04====
Chelsea finished second in the [[2003–04 FA Premier League]] and were eliminated by [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] in the semi-finals of the [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2004-05-05 |title=Chelsea 2-2 Monaco |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/champions_league/3680039.stm |access-date=2025-06-22 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

====2004–05====
Following the sacking of Ranieri and his succession by [[José Mourinho]], Makélélé was a key player in Chelsea's successful [[2004–05 Chelsea F.C. season|2004–05 season]], winning both the [[2004–05 FA Premier League|FA Premier League]] and the [[2004–05 Football League Cup|League Cup]]. His defensive qualities allowed the likes of [[Frank Lampard]], [[Joe Cole]], [[Arjen Robben]], [[Damien Duff]], [[Eiður Guðjohnsen]] and [[Didier Drogba]] to parade their attacking skills. Makélélé's importance was recognised by Mourinho, who declared him Chelsea's "Player of the Year".<ref>{{Cite web |title=How Claude Makelele changed English football |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/02/18/how-claude-makelele-changed-english-football |access-date=2021-07-12 |website=ChelseaFC}}</ref>

To cap off the 2004–05 season for the Frenchman, he was allowed to take a penalty awarded to Chelsea in the game against [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] on the day the Premier League trophy was due to be presented. Charlton goalkeeper [[Stephan Andersen]] saved it, but Makélélé scored on the rebound.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4501117.stm |title=Chelsea 1–0 Charlton |publisher=BBC Sport |date=7 May 2005 |access-date=16 August 2009}}</ref> In September 2005, he was selected as a member of the World XI at the [[FIFPro]] awards. The team was chosen by a vote of professional footballers in 40 countries. He added to his sizeable medal haul the following season, winning both the [[FA Community Shield]] and the Premier League.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Trophy Cabinet |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/about-chelsea/history/trophy-cabinet |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180524195503/https://www.chelseafc.com/en/about-chelsea/history/trophy-cabinet |archive-date=24 May 2018 |access-date=2020-06-29 |website=ChelseaFC}}</ref>

====2005–06====
In March 2006, [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] defeated Chelsea 1–0 in a Premier League game in which Fulham manager [[Chris Coleman (footballer)|Chris Coleman]]'s tactics centered on bypassing Makélélé on the wings when Fulham had possession and putting midfielders on Makélélé when Chelsea were in possession. With Makélélé struggling to function effectively, Chelsea lost the game. Coleman later explained that Makélélé was more than a mere defensive midfielder; that he was actually Chelsea's deep-lying playmaker, and that Chelsea's attacks were channelled through him. Thus, denying him possession was instrumental in unravelling Chelsea. Mourinho was subsequently forced to counter this tactic by withdrawing Lampard and [[Michael Essien]] further back in midfield to relieve the pressure on Makélélé.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.sportinglife.com/football/premiership/fulham/news/story_get.cgi?STORY_NAME=soccer/06/03/20/SOCCER_Fulham_Coleman.html&TEAMHD=fulham |title=Stop Makelele, Stop Chelsea – Coleman |first=Matt |last=Barlow |website=Sporting Life |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930050236/http://www.sportinglife.com/football/premiership/fulham/news/story_get.cgi?STORY_NAME=soccer%2F06%2F03%2F20%2FSOCCER_Fulham_Coleman.html&TEAMHD=fulham |archive-date=30 September 2007 |access-date=10 April 2019 |url-status=live |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

====2006–07====
On 5 November 2006, in a league encounter with [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], Makélélé scored his second goal for the club, a difficult curling volley from the edge of the 18-yard box which sped past goalkeeper [[Paul Robinson (footballer, born 1979)|Paul Robinson]] into the left-hand side of the goal to cue a bench-clearing celebration.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=199191&cc=5739&league=ENG.1 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120716150327/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=199191&cc=5739&league=ENG.1 |url-status=dead |archive-date=16 July 2012 |title=Tottenham 2–1 Chelsea |date=5 November 2006 |website=ESPN Soccernet |access-date=17 July 2010}}</ref>

On 5 December 2006, in a League Cup game against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], Makélélé wore the captain's armband in [[John Terry]]'s absence and with Frank Lampard rested. Makélélé was substituted at half-time for Lampard. Makélélé also wore the captain's armband the following season, when Terry, Lampard, and [[Michael Ballack]] were all unavailable.{{citation needed|date=January 2019}}

====2007–08====
The [[2007–08 Chelsea F.C. season|2007–08 season]] was a period of renaissance for the 35-year-old Makélélé, as he played in the majority of Chelsea's fixtures. Despite an ear infection that made him miss an early part of the season, he regained his place and forced Michael Essien into the [[right-back]] position, effectively pushing [[Juliano Belletti]] out of the team. Makélélé was instrumental in Chelsea's run to the [[2008 UEFA Champions League Final]] under the guidance of manager [[Avram Grant]]; the team were defeated by [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in a penalty-shootout, after a 1–1 deadlock following both regulation and extra time.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2008-05-22|title=Man Utd earn dramatic Euro glory|language=en-GB|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/7406252.stm|access-date=2020-06-29}}</ref>

===Paris Saint-Germain===
[[File:DKiev-PSG (7).jpg|thumb|upright|Makélélé with [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] in 2009]]
On 18 July 2008, it was reported that Makélélé was about to take a medical the following day in Paris ahead of a proposed move back to French football. On 21 July, Chelsea announced they had released Makélélé on a free transfer, while [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] confirmed that the player would join them and would be unveiled at a press conference that afternoon.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7516798.stm |title=Makelele leaves Chelsea for PSG |publisher=BBC Sport |date=21 July 2008 |access-date=26 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Makélélé leaves Chelsea to link up with PSG |url=http://fourfourtwo.com/news/england/13239/default.aspx |website=FourFourTwo |publisher=Future |access-date=21 July 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120312145406/http://fourfourtwo.com/news/england/13239/default.aspx |archive-date=12 March 2012 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

On 25 February 2010, he announced that he would retire at the end of the season, but in June, he retracted his statement and re-signed with PSG for an additional season.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11820_5979981,00.html |title=Makelele to hang up boots |publisher=Sky Sports |date=25 February 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131021113643/http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11820_5979981,00.html |archive-date=21 October 2013}}</ref> He won the [[2009–10 Coupe de France|Coupe de France]] with PSG at the end of the [[2009–10 Paris Saint-Germain F.C. season|2009–10 season]]. He later retired at the end of the campaign. The next season, he was appointed the assistant manager to [[Carlo Ancelotti]], who had just joined PSG from Makélélé's previous club, Chelsea.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Former France international Claude Makelele to become Carlo Ancelotti's assistant at Paris Saint-Germain - report |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506104240/https://www.goal.com/en/news/90/french-football/2011/12/30/2823687/former-france-international-claude-makelele-to-become-carlo |archive-date=6 May 2021 |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/90/french-football/2011/12/30/2823687/former-france-international-claude-makelele-to-become-carlo |date=30 Dec 2011 |website=goal.com}}</ref>

==International career==
Makélélé was first [[Cap (association football)|capped]] for [[France national football team|France]] in a match against [[Norway national football team|Norway]] in July 1995,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://archive.thedailystar.net/2003/09/02/d30902041645.htm |title=Finally Makelele |newspaper=The Daily Star |location=Dhaka |date=2 September 2003 |access-date=17 August 2014 |archive-date=19 August 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140819083004/http://archive.thedailystar.net/2003/09/02/d30902041645.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> and went on to represent his country at the [[Football at the 1996 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|1996 Summer Olympics]].{{citation needed|date=January 2019}}

Makélélé was not selected for France's [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998 World Cup]] and [[UEFA Euro 2000|Euro 2000]] successes, making his tournament debut at the [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002 World Cup]], where he started the team's final [[2002 FIFA World Cup Group A|Group A]] match against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]]. Under [[Jacques Santini]], Makélélé was a first-choice player in midfield at [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]], starting in three of France's four matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2004/matches/round=1581/match=1059167/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120120043501/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2004/matches/round=1581/match=1059167/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=20 January 2012|title=Zidane strikes stun England as France fight back|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=14 June 2004|access-date=27 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2004/matches/round=1581/match=1059183/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120120023832/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2004/matches/round=1581/match=1059183/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=20 January 2012|title=Henry makes the difference for France|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=22 June 2004|access-date=27 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2004/matches/round=1582/match=1059189/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120203073128/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2004/matches/round=1582/match=1059189/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 February 2012|title=Slick Greece shock EURO holders France|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=25 June 2004|access-date=27 August 2019}}</ref>

Makélélé decided to retire from international football in September 2004 in order to focus on club football with Chelsea, but 11 months later, in August 2005, he and compatriots Zinedine Zidane and Lilian Thuram were persuaded out of retirement by national team manager [[Raymond Domenech]], who coached Makélélé in the [[France national under-21 football team|France U21]] team over a decade prior, to help France qualify for the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]] in Germany.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Staff |date=2005-08-03 |title=Zidane and Makelele return to Les Bleus |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/aug/03/newsstory.sport8 |access-date=2025-06-22 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

As a member of the France squad competing at the 2006 World Cup, Makélélé's performances as a tireless midfield spoiler were invaluable to France's progress to the final as they defeated [[Spain national football team|Spain]], the defending champions [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] and Euro 2004 finalists [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] in the knock-out rounds. His partnership with [[Patrick Vieira]] in the defensive midfield proved effective as the team conceded only three goals in seven games and took four clean-sheets, a tally only bested by world champions [[Italy national football team|Italy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2006/5060036.stm|title=World Cup 2006 statistics|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 July 2005|access-date=27 August 2019}}</ref>

After a defeat to Italy on penalties in the [[2006 FIFA World Cup Final|World Cup Final]], Makélélé initially commented that he was again going to retire from international football. However, he was called up to the squad by Domenech for qualification matches for [[UEFA Euro 2008|Euro 2008]] against [[Georgia national football team|Georgia]] and Italy. On being asked about Makélélé being called up to his national squad despite being retired during an interview on [[Sky Sports]], Chelsea manager José Mourinho accused the French manager of treating Makélélé like a slave and refusing to honour his retirement. Mourinho said Domenech "has been very objective – very objective – and said you have to play Georgia and you have to play Italy. Makélélé wants to retire but the national coach won't allow him to retire."<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Hughes |first=Rob |date=2006-08-29 |title=Soccer: Makelele is free to make his choice - Sports - International Herald Tribune |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/08/29/sports/29iht-soccer.2630407.html |access-date=2025-06-22 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> [[FIFA]] confirmed that any club that refuses to release a player for national team duty is barred from using the player for two matches, a rule which is intended to discourage clubs from pretending that the player is injured.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Brodkin |first=Jon |date=2006-08-28 |title=Conciliatory Makelele says he is ready to turn out for France |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/aug/29/newsstory.sport3 |access-date=2025-06-22 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> On the same evening as the Mourinho interview, Makélélé told French TV station TPS Star, "Even if my club doesn't agree, I will humbly honor the call."<ref name=":1" />

Makélélé went on to continue playing with the France national team through the qualifications and then the finals for the Euro 2008 tournament, where France exited in the group stage after finishing bottom of their group. He and Thuram announced their retirement from international football on 17 June 2008, after France's 2–0 defeat to Italy.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/euro2008/story/0,23063,11966_3705170,00.html|title=France duo call it quits|date=18 June 2008|access-date=18 June 2007|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121209024719/http://www.skysports.com/football/euro2008/story/0,23063,11966_3705170,00.html|archive-date=9 December 2012|publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref>

==Style of play==
{{inline|section|date=May 2025}}
[[File:Avropa Liqası Muzeyi Bakıda 31.jpg|thumb|upright|A shirt worn by Makélélé at PSG]]
Regarded as one of the best players ever in his position, Makélélé revolutionised the role of the [[defensive midfielder]] in the Premier League; as such, this position frequently came to be known colloquially as "the Makélélé role" in England. A combative and hard-working player, although he was capable of getting forward and playing in more advanced positions, he usually played in front of his team's back-line, where he mainly served as a defensive foil for his more offensive teammates, due to his aggressive tackling, as well as his ability to read the game, break down plays, mark and anticipate opponents, and time his challenges. In this role, he was known in particular for his acceleration, positional sense, tactical discipline, intelligence, energy, and ball-winning ability; although he was not the fastest, most talented, technically skilled player on the ball, or particularly good in the air, he was also highly regarded throughout his career for being capable of functioning as a [[deep-lying playmaker]] for his team, due to his ability to dictate the tempo of his team's play in midfield with his short, efficient passing game, which allowed him to link up the defence with the attack effectively after winning back possession. His physical strength in spite of his small stature, combined with his low [[Center of mass|centre of gravity]], also gave him excellent balance on the ball in limited spaces, which allowed him to retain possession against more physical opponents. In addition to his defensive skills, Makélélé was also known for his tenacity, awareness, consistency, and strong mentality.<ref name="Makelele role"/><ref name=zonalmarking/><ref name=pyramid/><ref name="Perez has parting shot at Makelele"/><ref name=fernandohierro/><ref name=battery/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/jan/23/newsstory.sport7 |title=Claude reigns |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=23 January 2005 |access-date=26 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/news/0221-0e908247b46c-2ddcbd6061e9-1000--snap-shot-chelsea-s-2005-title-winners-a-decade-on/ |title=Snap shot: Chelsea's 2005 title winners a decade on |publisher=UEFA |date=3 May 2015 |access-date=13 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://archive.nytimes.com/www.nytimes.com/iht/2006/07/08/sports/IHT-08wcplayers.html |title=France and Italy – Settled and Similar |first=Peter |last=Berlin |newspaper=The New York Times |date=8 July 2006 |access-date=26 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.worldsoccer.com/uncategorized/the-hidden-depths-of-the-defensive-midfielder-333362 |title=The hidden depths of the defensive midfielder |first=Jamie |last=Rainbow |website=World Soccer |publisher=TI Media |date=14 January 2012 |access-date=28 February 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/barclays-premier-league/23/blog/post/2935772/premier-league-disappointing-lack-of-deep-lying-playmakers |title=Disappointing lack of deep-lying playmakers in the Premier League |first=Michael |last=Cox |publisher=ESPN |date=23 August 2016 |access-date=26 January 2019}}</ref> [[Jonathan Wilson (writer)|Jonathan Wilson]], when writing for ''[[The Guardian]]'' in 2013, labelled Makélélé as a type of [[holding midfielder]] he described as a "destroyer" - a player who is primarily tasked with running, winning back possession, and distributing the ball to other players.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2013/dec/18/question-holding-midfielders-changing-role|title=The Question: what does the changing role of holding midfielders tell us?|work=[[The Guardian]]|last=Wilson|first=Jonathan|author-link=Jonathan Wilson (writer)|date=18 December 2013|access-date=31 October 2014}}</ref>

==Managerial career==
[[File:Claude Makelele, staff PSG.JPG|thumb|upright|Makélélé in 2013, in his coaching role at Paris Saint-Germain]]
Makélélé became head coach of [[SC Bastia|Bastia]] on 24 May 2014. After less than six months in charge, however, he was dismissed on 3 November 2014 following a 1–0 defeat to [[En Avant Guingamp|Guingamp]] on 1 November, due to his inability to make an impact on the club as coach.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=2014-05-24 |title=Claude Makelele leaves Paris St-Germain post to coach Bastia |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/27559631 |access-date=2025-06-22 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Prior to Bastia, Makélélé was an assistant coach at Paris Saint-Germain alongside [[Paul Clement (football manager)|Paul Clement]]. In January 2016, Monaco appointed Makélélé as technical director.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Claude Makelele appointed Technical Director {{!}} News {{!}} AS Monaco FC |url=http://www.asmonaco.com/en/article/claude-makelele-appointed-technical-director-69744.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010104548/http://www.asmonaco.com/en/article/claude-makelele-appointed-technical-director-69744.html |archive-date=2017-10-10 |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=www.asmonaco.com |language=en-EN}}</ref> Makélélé joined Clement as his assistant coach at Premier League club [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] in January 2017.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-01-11 |title=Swansea City appoint Claude Makelele as their assistant manager |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/38588997 |access-date=2025-06-22 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Makélélé then joined Belgian side [[K.A.S. Eupen|Eupen]] as their head coach in November 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Makelele leaves Swans |url=https://www.swanseacity.com/news/makelele-leaves-swans |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=www.swanseacity.com |language=en}}</ref> He left Eupen in August 2019 after almost two full seasons as head coach to return to his former club Chelsea as a youth coach and technical mentor.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Claude Makelele returns to Chelsea in a new coaching role |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/claude-makelele-returns-to-chelsea-in-a-new-coaching-role |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=www.chelseafc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> 

In September 2023, Makélélé left his coaching role at Chelsea by mutual decision.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-26 |title=Chelsea exits continue as Claude Makelele leaves coaching role |url=https://talksport.com/football/1578588/claude-makelele-leaves-chelsea-mutual-decision/ |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=talkSPORT |language=en-gb}}</ref> He was appointed head coach of Greece's club [[Asteras Tripolis F.C.|Asteras Tripolis]] on 14 September 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-10 |title=Ο σπουδαίος Claude Makélélé προπονητής του ASTERAS AKTOR! |trans-title=The great Claude Makélélé coach of ASTERAS AKTOR! |url=https://asterastripolis.gr/first-team/4670-o-spoudaios-claude-makelele-proponitis-tou-asteras-aktor.html |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=Αστέρας Τρίπολης - Ο σπουδαίος Claude Makélélé προπονητής του ASTERAS AKTOR!}}</ref> Caretaker manager [[Savvas Pantelidis]] had coached the team in a 1–3 loss against [[Atromitos F.C.|Atromitos]] the day after Makélélé's appointment, with the latter watching from the stands. In a surprise announcement, Makélélé left the club after three weeks and as many games, allegedly over board interference in his squad selections and tactics. He was unbeaten in his games in charge. Pantelidis would eventually succeed him as manager three days later.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Claude Makelele quitte son poste d'entraîneur de l'Asteras Tripolis après seulement trois matches |trans-title=Claude Makelele leaves his coaching position at Asteras Tripolis after only three matches |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Claude-makelele-quitte-son-poste-d-entraineur-de-l-asteras-tripolis-apres-seulement-trois-matches/1512472 |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=L'Équipe |language=fr}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In the spring of 2004, Makélélé began dating French model [[Noémie Lenoir]]. Lenoir gave birth to a boy, Kelyan (born 24 January 2005). The couple split in early 2009. Despite widespread reports that Lenoir was married to Makélélé, she wrote a blog in 2009 clarifying their former relationship, saying, "I'm not and have never been married. I do have a son. I have a wonderful baby's father and have a great relationship with him, however I've been single for some time now."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/3am/celebrity-news/noemie-lenoir-10-things-you-221023|title=Noemie Lenoir: 10 things you need to know about the French model|website=[[Daily Mirror]] |date=13 May 2010}}</ref>{{better source needed|reason=tabloid|date=May 2026}}

In May 2010, Lenoir attempted to commit suicide outside Makélélé's Paris home by ingesting a lethal amount of drugs and alcohol. Lenoir has had a long battle with substance abuse and later checked into rehab.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/news/mamps-model-noemie-lenoir-recovers-after-suicide-bid-1972479.html |title=M&S model Noemie Lenoir recovers after 'suicide bid' |first1=Katie |last1=Hodge |first2=Josie |last2=Clarke |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |date=13 May 2010}}</ref>

Claude has a son named Kaïys born in 2010. Kaïys Makelele who was previously with Juventus in Los Angeles, is currently playing football in Barcelona.
